text:
San Jose was outplayed for most of the night and still won it. FLA led in expected goals 3.99 to 3.56 and in shot attempts 70 to 61, and the model gave them a 57 percent share of simulated replays, against 43 for SJS. The Sharks took a 3-0 lead anyway, then needed overtime to finish it, as Luca Cagnoni scored at 3:14 of the extra period for a 4-3 win.

Will Smith did the damage early. Mason Marchment opened the scoring in the first period on a 2 percent chance, and Smith followed with two goals in the second: a shorthanded wrist shot at 5:52, then a power-play slap shot at 10:37 on a 72 percent look. Macklin Celebrini assisted on both and finished with three assists and seven shots on goal. Smith's line controlled the ice, with SJS holding a 2.5 to 0.29 edge in expected goals while he was out there.

FLA pushed back. Eetu Luostarinen scored on a second-period power play, then added a tip-in at 5:01 of the third, and Matthew Tkachuk tied it just 17 seconds later. FLA out-chanced SJS 1.20 to 0.50 in the third, and Sam Bennett had a 33 percent look that Yaroslav Askarov stopped. That save mattered: Askarov was about one goal better than the shots he faced deserved. In overtime, SJS held a 0.91 to 0.00 edge in expected goals, and Cagnoni, assisted by Smith and Celebrini, ended it.
